title: Argentine-ant regional distribution · GABI snapshot
datasetTitle: Data supporting: The global spread and invasion capacities of alien ants
observationPeriod: Individual observation dates are not supplied; GABI extraction on 15 June 2022
method: Filter Dataset 1 for exact source taxon Linepithema.humile; join Dataset 2 by exact region name. Preserve every reported status and note.
precision: One published regional reference anchor per geographic region; not GPS occurrence points, nest locations, range boundaries, or current status.

statusDefinitions.native: Reported by this dataset as within the species native region.
statusDefinitions.established.outdoors: Recorded in the wild outside a reported native region.
statusDefinitions.established.indoors: Recorded in indoor settings such as buildings or greenhouses outside a reported native region.
statusDefinitions.border.interception: Recorded from border interception outside a reported native region; not proof of establishment.

classificationPolicy: Display reported classifications without editorial reclassification. Broad South and Central American regional labels can differ from narrower native-range treatments; a native label for a region does not establish that every part of that region is native range.
caveats: This is a fixed 2022 database snapshot published in 2023, not current or live observations.
Regional anchors locate the named regions only. Marker position does not locate an ant record, simulated nest, or battlefront.
Presence and establishment categories do not identify supercolonies or establish cooperation, aggression, fronts, or alliances.
Individual observation dates, exact collection coordinates, and record-level literature citations are not included in these deposited CSVs; underlying references are available from GABI.
Do not infer absence from a missing regional row; surveillance and reporting vary.
Dataset CC BY 4.0 is independently declared on Figshare. No journal figure, Antmaps screenshot, or Antmaps geometry is redistributed.
transformations: Exact taxon filtering; one-to-one region-name join; numeric latitude/longitude parsing.
Original region, status, note and realm retained without scientific reclassification.
Stable ASCII IDs added; source attribution and regional-anchor precision labels added.
No geographic boundary geometry inferred from reference coordinates.

relatedRecognitionStudies.title: The Effect of Diet on Colony Recognition and Cuticular Hydrocarbon Profiles of the Invasive Argentine Ant, Linepithema humile
relatedRecognitionStudies.observationPeriod: Calendar collection dates not reported in article; behavioral experiment spans ten weeks
relatedRecognitionStudies.method: Paired-worker behavioral assays comparing dietary-treatment nests from UC Irvine CAL with Mason Regional Park CAL and Lake Skinner LS reference workers.
relatedRecognitionStudies.finding: Field feeding treatments preserved tolerance toward same-CAL reference ants and aggression toward Lake Skinner workers. Food similarity alone did not merge these colonies.
relatedRecognitionStudies.caveat: No calendar observation year is asserted. These local pairings do not refresh the 2008–2009 Berkeley–Lake Hodges or cross-continental comparisons.
relatedRecognitionStudies.reuse: Original concise text only; no article figure or experimental data asset copied.

relatedRecognitionStudies.title: Long-term spread of Argentine ant (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) European supercolonies on three Mediterranean islands
relatedRecognitionStudies.observationPeriod: Ibiza and Formentera: 2004 and August–September 2016; Corsica: 2007–2008, with identity drawn from prior literature
relatedRecognitionStudies.method: Island beach surveys; Main/Catalonian identity at Ibiza and Formentera assessed through paired aggression assays against reference populations.
relatedRecognitionStudies.finding: Sampled island populations included distinct Main and Catalonian identities. Regional occurrence and recognition were measured separately.
relatedRecognitionStudies.caveat: The 2021 publication does not make these observations current. Corsican membership was taken from earlier literature, not new 2021 aggression assays. No new California comparison was tested.
relatedRecognitionStudies.reuse: Original concise text only; no map, aerial background, or article figure copied.

relatedRecognitionStudies.title: Undesirable dispersal via a river pathway of a single Argentine ant supercolony newly invading an inland urban area of Japan
relatedRecognitionStudies.observationPeriod: Distribution survey July–December 2022; aggression assays September–December 2022
relatedRecognitionStudies.method: Five-on-five aggression assays comparing Nara workers with Kobe LH1, LH2, LH3 and LH4 reference populations; 522 trials per reference pairing.
relatedRecognitionStudies.finding: Nara workers tolerated Kobe LH2 workers and showed strong aggression toward LH1, LH3 and LH4 reference workers, supporting an LH2 identity for the sampled Nara population.
relatedRecognitionStudies.caveat: This is local 2022 evidence, not a new California–Japan comparison. Its Google Maps-backed figure is not a rights-cleared geographic asset for this game.
relatedRecognitionStudies.reuse: Original concise text only; no article figure or Google Maps background copied.
